title: Peptides with antioxidant and antibacterial potential in anion‐exchange fractions of pepsin‐hydrolyzed IPB‐D1 chicken egg white
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

The IPB-D1 chicken, an indigenous breed from Indonesia, is a potentially valuable but insufficiently studied source of bioactive peptides. Egg white proteins from this breed may yield peptides with antioxidant and antibacterial properties, which are of interest for functional food and biomedical applications.

RESULTS

Egg white proteins were subjected to pepsin enzymatic hydrolysis, followed by ultrafiltration and anion-exchange chromatography, to obtain peptide fractions. Antioxidant capacity was determined using a 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical scavenging assay and expressed both as scavenging activity (%SA) and vitamin C equivalents (EVC, mg g−1 protein). Antibacterial activity was tested against Bacillus cereus, Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Salmonella Typhi using the disc diffusion method. The most negatively charged fraction (AF2) exhibited the highest antioxidant activity (14.30 ± 0.71% SA, equivalent to 10.18 ± 0.94 mg EVC g−1 protein). In contrast, fraction AF1 showed the strongest antibacterial activity against most tested pathogens.

CONCLUSION

Charge-based fractionation enhanced the bioactivity of IPB-D1 egg white peptides effectively. These results highlight the potential of IPB-D1 chicken egg white as a novel source of functional peptides with antioxidant and antibacterial effects for applications in the food and health industries. © 2025 Society of Chemical Industry.
